profile.headline: Software Engineer
profile.summary:
I've always been a bit of a nerd.

Growing up in New England, I had a love of abstract ideas and complex concepts, from sci-fi to cosmology, and that passion eventually led me to studying physics. I’ve always enjoyed problem-solving, and the logical nature of math, so it seemed like a natural fit. I graduated in 2019 with a B.S. in physics, but finding a job in the industry was another matter entirely. I decided to pivot to software engineering, as I had taken a few classes in school, and enjoyed them immensely. In the spring of 2020, I attended a “coding bootcamp” called Revature, in a full-stack web development program using the .Net tech stack. But with the lockdowns that came that fateful summer, many job opportunities dried up.

I eventually took a supervisor position at Walmart, and ended up learning a lot more than I expected to. This was my first official position of leadership, and it taught me so much about the added responsibilities that came with it. I had been a team-lead on 2 group projects at Revature, which certainly helped, but this was a new challenge altogether. It really grew my respect for the managers I'd had in the past and the types of pressures they faced.

In early 2022, I heard about a new school, in Tulsa, called Holberton. They have a much more in-depth full-stack program here, where I'm getting a lot of hands-on experience with a number of languages and frameworks, such as Python, C, Javascript, mysql, Node.js, React, and more.

With my soft skills and technical expertise combined, I offer a unique package. That of a nerd who can program and translate the most complex of data. But also one with enough life experience to relate and communicate with anyone, be it as a team-member or leader. I've always felt like a man with a foot in 2 worlds, in more ways than one, but now I think that just gives me a more well-rounded perspective.

projects.title: Star Trek Episodes API
projects.description:
A Node/Express API server with a MySql db, serving every episode of Star Trek.
Searchable by show, title, date, season, and episode.
Also handles Authentication and Pagination.

https://github.com/PStewart1/Lost-in-SPAAACE
